subject: community-medicine
title: Disability Limitation, Rehabilitation, Impairment and Handicap

steps.title: The sequence from disease to handicap
steps.tx: Learn the chain in order: **disease** leads to impairment, impairment to disability, and disability to handicap. An accident illustrates each link: the injury is the disorder, loss of a foot is the impairment, inability to walk is the disability, and unemployment that follows is the handicap. Each link invites a different intervention, which the next steps separate.
steps.say: Memorise the chain in order. Disease brings impairment, impairment brings disability, disability brings handicap. An accident shows it clearly: injury, lost foot, cannot walk, loses the job. Each link needs a different response.

steps.tx: An accident lays out **disease to handicap** in four ordered boxes. The injury is the disorder that starts the sequence. Loss of the foot is the impairment, meaning the anatomical deficit left behind. Being unable to walk is the disability, the function that has gone. Unemployment that then follows is the handicap, a social disadvantage. Each box invites a different action, and later steps keep those actions apart.

steps.title: Impairment: loss of structure or function
steps.tx: **Impairment** means any loss or abnormality of psychological, physiological or anatomical structure or function, such as a lost foot, defective vision or intellectual disability. It may be visible or invisible, temporary or permanent, progressive or regressive. One impairment can breed another: nerve damage in leprosy, the primary impairment, leads to plantar ulcers as a secondary impairment.
steps.say: First link means loss of structure or function. A lost foot, defective vision or intellectual disability all qualify. Impairments can hide or show, pass or persist, even breed secondary ones, as leprosy nerve damage leads to plantar ulcers.

rows: Visible, like limb loss, or invisible, like pain pathways

steps.title: Disability: activity beyond normal range
steps.tx: **Disability** means restriction or lack of ability to perform an activity in the manner or within the range considered normal for a human being, resulting from an impairment. Difficulty seeing, hearing, walking, writing or speaking all qualify. Modern usage treats disability as an umbrella term covering impairments, activity limitations and participation restrictions together.
steps.say: Second link concerns activity. The person cannot perform an activity in the normal manner or range: seeing, hearing, walking, writing or speaking. Modern usage widens the word into an umbrella over impairment, activity limits and participation limits.

steps.title: Handicap: the social disadvantage
steps.tx: **Handicap** means a disadvantage resulting from impairment or disability that limits or prevents fulfilment of a role normal for that person by age, sex and social and cultural factors. A disability becomes a handicap only when it blocks what society expects at that life stage. The term has since been dropped from current classifications, a favourite exam footnote.
steps.say: Third link is social. Disadvantage blocks the role expected at that age and in that culture, like work expected of an adult. A disability turns into this only when it blocks expected roles. Note the footnote: current classifications have dropped the term.

right.title: Handicap adds society
points: Measured against age and social role

steps.title: Disability limitation in late presentation
steps.tx: **Disability limitation** applies when a patient reports late in pathogenesis, aiming to prevent or halt the move from impairment toward handicap. Intense, adequate treatment at this stage can still arrest the process: cataract surgery restores sight, glaucoma treatment saves remaining vision, and leprosy therapy prevents deformity. Reporting late narrows, but does not erase, what treatment can win back.
steps.say: Late presentation still leaves room to act. Adequate treatment here halts the slide from impairment toward handicap. Cataract surgery restores sight, glaucoma care saves remaining vision, leprosy therapy prevents deformity. Late narrows the winnings; it does not erase them.

steps.title: Disability prevention across all levels
steps.tx: **Disability prevention** spans every level: immunisation against polio reduces impairment occurrence at the primary level, appropriate treatment limits disability at the secondary level, and rehabilitation prevents disability hardening into handicap at the tertiary level. Communicable diseases, malnutrition, poor perinatal care and accidents cause about 70 percent of disabling impairments in developing countries, so primary action dominates.
steps.say: Prevention of disability uses every level. Polio vaccine stops impairment arising, good treatment limits disability, rehabilitation stops handicap forming. Since infections, malnutrition, poor perinatal care and accidents cause most cases in developing countries, primary action dominates.

steps.title: Rehabilitation defined by restoration
steps.tx: **Rehabilitation** means the combined and coordinated use of medical, social, educational and vocational measures to train or retrain a person to the highest possible level of functional ability. Its test is social integration: active participation in mainstream community life. Care therefore continues after fever settles and stitches come out, until the person lives and works to the hilt of capacity.
steps.say: Restoration defines this stage. Medical, social, educational and vocational measures combine to train the person toward the highest reachable function. Social integration is the test. Care ends not when stitches come out, but when the person lives and works to full capacity.

steps.tx: Four professions share **community rehabilitation**, medical care, vocational retraining, social support and psychological help, arranged so the person reaches the highest functional level still open. The wheel puts those efforts around one patient who is returning to ordinary community life. Success is active participation, not a healed wound: living and working to the limit of remaining capacity once fever has settled and sutures are out.

steps.title: Four areas of rehabilitation
steps.tx: Rehabilitation works in four areas: **medical rehabilitation** restores function, vocational rehabilitation restores capacity to earn a livelihood, social rehabilitation restores family and social relationships, and psychological rehabilitation restores personal dignity and confidence. Teams add physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, audiology, psychology, education, social work and vocational guidance around the physician.
steps.say: Four areas organise the work. Medical care restores function, vocational training restores earning, social work restores relationships, psychological support restores dignity and confidence. Therapists, educators and vocational counsellors join the physician around the patient.

steps.title: Examples examiners quote
steps.tx: Quoted examples include **schools for the blind**, aids for people with limb loss, reconstructive surgery in leprosy, muscle re-education and graded exercises after neurological disorders, and change of profession where the old job no longer fits. Each example pairs a stabilised disability with a route back into ordinary life, which is exactly what the definition demands.
steps.say: Anchor the definition with examples. Schools for the blind, aids after limb loss, reconstructive surgery in leprosy, graded exercises after nerve injury, and a changed profession all pair lasting disability with a route back into ordinary life.
